sections.heading: Asking that my days would actually matter
sections.text: Lord, more time will not do me any good unless I live it with you, for you, and in a way that honours you. As this year begins, do not let me measure my life only by how long it lasts, how much I get done, or what I manage to gain. Teach me to receive each day as a gift meant to be lived in your presence and offered back to you.
theological_themes: Life is only truly fruitful when lived before God and for his glory.
Time is a gift to be stewarded, not merely accumulated.
The believer’s ordinary days belong to God.

scripture_references.connection: Moses asks God to teach his people to number their days so they may live wisely. That grounds the prayer’s desire to treat the coming year as a sacred trust rather than a mere extension of time.
Paul teaches that even ordinary actions are to be done for God’s glory. This supports the prayer’s aim that every day and every part of life be directed toward honouring God.

sections.heading: Depending on grace for every hour
sections.text: Give me grace before I know I need it, grace while I am in the middle of need, and grace after I have failed or obeyed. Let your grace lead me, hold me up, correct me, cleanse me, and help me in every hour. Keep me from drifting away from you even for a moment. Holy Spirit, shape my thoughts, guard my words, direct my steps, make my work fruitful for your purposes, strengthen even the smallest beginnings of faith in me, and make me want to live so that your goodness can be seen.
theological_themes: God’s grace is needed at every stage of obedience and weakness.
The Holy Spirit actively guides, strengthens, and sanctifies the believer.
Faith, speech, work, and witness all depend on God’s help.

scripture_references.connection: Jesus teaches that his disciples cannot bear fruit apart from abiding in him. This directly supports the prayer’s dependence on God for every thought, word, step, work, and growth in faith.
Paul describes life by the Spirit as the way believers resist the flesh and bear godly fruit. This grounds the request for the Spirit to guide and sanctify the whole life.
Christ tells Paul that his grace is sufficient and his power is made perfect in weakness. That supports the prayer’s repeated dependence on grace for sustaining help in every hour.

sections.heading: Setting out into an unknown year with the Triune God
sections.text: I do not know what this year will hold. I feel like a small boat leaving shore for waters I have never crossed. Father, be my safe home and the harbour I can always return to. Lord Jesus, steer me when I cannot see the way. Holy Spirit, fill what is empty in me and move me forward in the strength you give. Lead me toward my final home with you, and keep me ready for whatever you call me to do. Keep my lamp lit, my ears open, my heart warm with love, and my soul free from the things that would bind it.
theological_themes: The future is unknown to the believer but not to God.
The Christian life is lived in fellowship with the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.
God guides his people toward their final home while calling them to readiness and obedience now.

scripture_references.connection: Paul’s blessing names the grace of Christ, the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit together in the life of believers. This supports the prayer’s explicitly Trinitarian trust at the start of the year.

This passage calls God’s people to trust him rather than their own understanding, with the promise that he will make their paths straight. It fits the prayer’s surrender to God’s guidance in an unknown future.

Jesus calls his servants to be dressed for action and to keep their lamps burning as they wait for their master. This is the biblical source behind the prayer’s desire to stay alert, responsive, and ready.

sections.heading: Being taught, steadied, and made joyful in your ways
sections.text: Give me the grace that makes me holy, the comfort that keeps me from losing heart, and the wisdom that teaches me what is true. Hold me by your strong hand. Instruct me by your counsel. Let your Word search me and correct me, not to crush me, but to bring me back into the light. Let your presence steady me when everything else feels uncertain. Make reverent awe of you the deep posture of my life, and let your victories—not my achievements—be my joy.
theological_themes: God sanctifies, comforts, teaches, guides, and steadies his people.
God’s Word rightly searches and judges the believer’s life.
Reverent fear of God and joy in his triumph belong together.

scripture_references.connection: The psalmist speaks of God holding him, guiding him with counsel, and afterward receiving him to glory. This closely supports the prayer’s requests for God’s hand, counsel, stabilizing presence, and final hope.
God’s Word is described as light for the path, which supports the request that God’s instruction direct and evaluate the way forward.
This passage presents God’s Word as living and discerning the thoughts and intentions of the heart. It grounds the prayer’s request for God’s law to judge or search the believer truthfully.

Paul describes God forgiving sins through Christ and triumphing over hostile powers through the cross. This supports the prayer’s desire to find joy not in personal success but in God’s decisive victories.

content_provenance.original_author: Unattributed Puritan source (compiled and edited by Arthur Bennett)
content_provenance.original_source: The Valley of Vision: A Collection of Puritan Prayers and Devotions, ed. Arthur Bennett (The Banner of Truth Trust)
content_provenance.source_copyright_status: Compilation, titles and arrangement in copyright (Banner of Truth, 1975); underlying Puritan sources are public domain.
content_provenance.modern_version_note: Contemporary prayer based on the theological themes and ideas of the historical source; not a reproduction of the original wording.

theological_issues_identified: The original phrase about God prospering every work could be misunderstood as a request for worldly success or guaranteed visible results. It has been rendered as fruitfulness for God’s purposes rather than personal achievement.
The request for God’s law to judge has been framed as Scripture searching, correcting, and bringing the believer into the light, not as condemnation for those who are in Christ.
The line about being guided to heaven carries a doctrine of perseverance and final hope. The modern version preserves that aim without implying escape from present earthly responsibilities.
significant_interpretive_choices: The nautical image was retained in contemporary language because it is central to the original’s movement into an unknown year with God as refuge, guide, and empowering presence.
The references to Father, Son, and Holy Spirit were kept explicitly Trinitarian rather than collapsed into a general statement about God’s help.

The phrase about having loins girded and a lamp burning was rendered as readiness for God’s call while retaining the concrete image of a lit lamp, since the wording alludes strongly to Jesus’ teaching in Luke 12.
The original’s ‘thy triumphs my joy’ was interpreted as joy in God’s victories, especially Christ’s victory over sin and hostile powers, rather than joy in the believer’s own successes.
